papers.title: HDAC1/2 maintain TERT mRNA stability in TERT-rearranged neuroblastoma
papers.abstract: Genomic TERT locus rearrangements define an aggressive high-risk neuroblastoma subgroup characterized by enhancer hijacking, high-level TERT expression and continuous telomerase activation. Although these structural alterations supply a strong transcriptional drive, the post-transcriptional mechanisms preserving TERT mRNA presence remain incompletely understood. We identified histone deacetylases 1 and 2 (HDAC1/2) as essential post-transcriptional guardians of TERT mRNA stability in TERT-rearranged neuroblastoma. Pharmacological inhibition or RNAi-mediated depletion of HDAC1 and HDAC2, but not HDACs 3-11, rapidly downregulated TERT transcript levels and suppressed telomerase enzymatic activity. Transcript decay kinetics following transcriptional arrest with actinomycin D confirmed that HDAC1/2 blockade accelerates TERT mRNA decay, reducing transcript half-life by 30-47%. High-resolution ChIP-seq profiling across the translocation breakpoint demonstrated HDAC inhibition does not alter local chromatin accessibility. Array-based DNA methylation profiling showed only a mild, non-specific global reduction in CpG island methylation upon panobinostat exposure and no focal correlation with TERT transcript loss across the breakpoint locus. Depleting TERT mRNA via HDAC1/2 inhibition dismantled a core 50-gene TERT-associated oncogenic expression network. Ectopic re-expression of TERT cDNA partially rescued cellular viability and normalized expression of key signature genes despite continuous HDAC inhibition. HDAC1/2 inhibition significantly attenuated tumor growth, reduced intratumor TERT expression and prolonging overall survival in both preventive and therapeutic TERT-rearranged xenograft mouse models. Our data establish a post-transcriptional rather than transcriptional mode of TERT regulation and confirm tumor suppression is partly driven by depleting TERT transcripts, uncovering a HDAC1/2 dependency in TERT-driven neuroblastoma. We provide a molecular rationale for therapeutic strategies disrupting HDAC1/2-mediated TERT mRNA stabilization.

papers.title: From Calcium-dependent currents to Multitarget Therapy: A Pharmacological Strategy for Glioblastoma
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive primary brain tumor with limited treatment options and substantial interpatient heterogeneity. Ion transport and cell-volume regulation may represent pharmacological vulnerabilities in glioma stem cells (GSCs). Here, we characterized membrane currents in patient-derived GSCs, identifying a calcium-dependent anion conductance consistent with volume-regulated anion channels (VRACs) and an inward current consistent with Na+/Ca++ exchanger exchanger (NCX) activity. Based on these findings, we investigated individual compounds and developed a multitarget cocktail comprising niflumic acid (NFA), bumetanide (BTN), and R-ketorolac (R-K) to target complementary mechanisms involved in ion homeostasis, cell-volume regulation, and cellular dynamics. The cocktail affected cell viability and mechanical properties and showed synergistic effects in U87 cells and patient-derived GSCs with similar electrophysiological profiles. Treatment did not measurably alter spontaneous activity in cultured hippocampal neurons but caused substantial HMC3 cytotoxicity. Encapsulation in transferrin-functionalized liposomes attenuated HMC3 toxicity while preserving activity against glioblastoma cells, suggesting a potential strategy to improve treatment selectivity. Further pharmacological studies identified a potential vulnerability associated with NCX activity, although its contribution to cytotoxicity remains unclear. Overall, our findings highlight electrophysiological heterogeneity in patient-derived GSCs and support further investigation of ion transport as a therapeutic target in GBM. Combining multitarget pharmacology with targeted drug delivery may help address heterogeneous treatment responses, although further studies are needed to establish the underlying mechanisms, safety, and vivo efficacy.

papers.title: High-throughput identification of changes in cellular localization for RNA-binding proteins during adenovirus infection reveals viral harnessing of nuclear speckles
papers.abstract: Adenovirus (AdV) is a human DNA virus reliant on host RNA processing machinery. While research into AdV has yielded landmark discoveries in RNA biology, studies investigating the scope of AdV dependency on specific host RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) are lacking. Here we performed optical pooled screening on a cell library where hundreds of RBPs are endogenously tagged. Pooled imaging followed by in situ barcode sequencing revealed a broad view of virus-induced host RBP relocalization patterns, including those recruited to viral replication compartments (VRCs). A targeted siRNA screen of relocalized RBPs demonstrated a requirement for the nuclear speckle (NS) core protein SON during virus infection. Depletion of SON resulted in reduced viral gene expression, impaired NS protein recruitment to early-stage VRCs, and impaired mobility of SRRM2 during infection. These findings suggest a crucial role of SON and NS functions in regulating viral gene expression and demonstrate the power of pooled tagging coupled to optical screening in investigating virus-host interactions.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics reveals organ-specific jasmonate signaling in Arabidopsis under combined heat and phosphate starvation
papers.abstract: Phosphate (Pi) limitation is a major constraint on plant productivity and is aggravated by heat stress. In nature, soil buffers air temperature, creating a vertical thermal gradient that shields roots from extreme heat; thus, heat and Pi starvation, although often co-occurring, are perceived mainly by different organs, shoots and roots respectively. How plants integrate these organ-specific stresses into a coordinated response remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how Arabidopsis responds to combined Pi deficiency and elevated temperature, using a root-zone temperature gradient and an integrated analysis of ion accumulation, phytohormone levels and transcriptomic profiles in roots and shoots. The combined stress elicited a distinct response that cannot be explained by the addition of individual stress effects. Jasmonate levels changed in an organ-specific manner, with JA-Ile accumulating in roots and JA declining in shoots, and mutants with reduced (jar1-1) or constitutive (jazQ) JA signaling showed altered transcriptional, growth and leaf-temperature responses. These results identify jasmonic acid (JA) as a modulator of the balance between acclimation and growth under combined nutritional and thermal limitation, advancing our understanding of how plants cope with the multi-stress scenarios driven by climate change.

papers.title: Maternal obesity disrupts glucose oxidation and mitochondrial fission in the myometrium at term gestation
papers.abstract: Women with obesity experience delayed spontaneous labor onset, slow labor progression, and elevated risk of labor dystocia, but the underlying mechanisms are poorly understood. We previously established a mouse model of diet-induced obesity that exhibits decreased uterine contractility, labor dystocia, and elevated fatty acids in the myometrium. Here, we used this model to determine how maternal obesity affects energy production and mitochondrial homeostasis in the myometrium at term. Myometrium tissue and myometrial smooth muscle cells from diet-induced obese mice at term showed decreased pyruvate utilization, inhibition of glucose oxidation, and disruption of mitochondrial fission and mitophagy. Treatment with medium-chain fatty acids in both murine and human primary myometrial cells resulted in significant decreases in abundance of mitochondrial fission proteins. Finally, mitochondrial spare capacity in human myometrial cells decreased with body mass index of the patient providing the cells. Taken together, these findings indicate that fatty acid accumulation dysregulates energy metabolism and mitochondrial homeostasis in the myometrium and may contribute to dysfunctional labor in women with obesity.

papers.title: GCase deficiency impairs uptake of α-synuclein-loaded ectosome by astrocytes
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) involves the prion-like propagation of -synuclein. One mechanism for the spread of -synuclein between neurons in PD is ectosomes. But PD is a multicellular disorder in which astrocytes also play a critical role. How astrocytes take up ectosomes and whether this is affected in PD is unclear. Here we show that GCase-deficiency, as occurs in PD, impairs astrocytic uptake of neuron-derived ectosomes containing -synuclein. The defect in ectosome uptake by astrocytes is driven by compromised macropinocytosis and can be rescued by reducing glucosylceramides or restoring lysosomal function. These findings identify sphingolipid metabolism as a key regulator of ectosome uptake by primary and iPSC-derived astrocytes. They also support a shift from the uptake and clearance of -synuclein by astrocytes in health, towards the transmission of -synuclein pathology towards neurons in PD.

papers.title: Quiescent Cells Exhibit a Senescence-Like Secretory Phenotype
papers.abstract: Cellular quiescence is traditionally considered a reversible state of cell cycle arrest, distinct from senescence, which is associated with a characteristic senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). However, whether quiescent cells exhibit a comparable secretory program remains poorly understood. Here, we identify and characterize a Quiescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype (QASP) by integrating single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing datasets from human fibroblasts and preadipocytes. We find that quiescent cells exhibit increased expression of genes encoding inflammatory mediators and extracellular matrix-associated proteins, with substantial overlap between the QASP and SASP. This transcriptional program is highly heterogeneous, varying across cell types, quiescence induction methods, and environmental oxygen levels. In particular, contact inhibition induces a stronger inflammatory signature than serum withdrawal in several cellular contexts. Multiplexed cytokine profiling demonstrated active secretion of inflammatory mediators, including IL-1{beta}, IL-6, IL-15, and CCL2, in quiescent fibroblasts, with secretion levels varying by induction method and generally higher following contact inhibition than serum withdrawal. Analysis of single-cell transcriptomic data from human lung tissue further reveals increased QASP-associated gene expression in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), particularly in myofibroblasts, linking this phenotype to inflammatory signaling and extracellular matrix remodeling. Together, these findings identify the QASP as a context-dependent secretory program that shares features with the SASP and may contribute to inflammatory signaling and extracellular matrix remodeling in both physiological and pathological conditions.

papers.title: Three novel deep-branching orphan protist lineages from the marine rare biosphere
papers.abstract: Metabarcoding has transformed our view of marine protist communities, yet many sequences in environmental surveys are not assigned confident taxonomic identity. These taxonomically ambiguous sequences may include lineages that are not within any known eukaryotic supergroup, which we refer to here as orphan lineages. These orphan lineages matter beyond taxonomy-based community analyses, because they can help us understand early eukaryotic evolution. Here we used phylogenetic inferences and sequence similarity networks (SSNs) of long-read metabarcoding data of the ribosomal operon (18S-28S rDNA) to identify three novel phylum-level orphan lineages. We designate these lineages Deep Orphan Lineages 1-3 (DEEPOLs) and show that they are exclusively marine and part of the rare biosphere, yet ecologically distinct: DEEPOL1 is a cosmopolitan generalist, DEEPOL2 a conditionally rare lineage capable of local polar blooms, and DEEPOL3 a non-polar lineage with a tendency toward the dark ocean. For DEEPOL2, lineage-specific digital PCR (dPCR) combined with catalyzed reporter deposition fluorescence in situ hybridization (CARD-FISH) provides the first in situ visualization of these cells, revealing small, flagellated, and morphologically inconspicuous protists. Together, our results show that substantial diversity remains hidden among rare lineages, and that long-read sequencing combined with targeted molecular and microscopy approaches offers a first step toward linking orphan sequences to organisms and their evolution and ecological roles.

papers.title: Single-cell genomics reveals genomic and functional differentiation between freshwater and saline Achromatium populations.
papers.abstract: Giant sulfur bacteria of the genus Achromatium reportedly contain extensive genomic diversity within individual cells. Most genomic data (35 assemblies) come from freshwater populations obtained from Lake Stechlin, Germany, alongside four single-cell genomes from a salt marsh and saline mineral springs. Here, we characterize marine Achromatium from mangrove sediments in Guadeloupe and compare them with freshwater and saline references. Microscopy, elemental mapping, and Raman spectroscopy revealed calcium-rich inclusions, and intracellular elemental sulfur as previously described for this genus. Scanning electron microscopy revealed two cell-size morphotypes. We generated eleven single-cell, four mixed-cell, and two metagenomic binned assemblies from Guadeloupe mangrove. Divergent copies of conserved marker genes revealed extensive intracellular genomic diversity in individual cells of both morphotypes. Multigene phylogenies provided separation between freshwater references and most genomes from saline environments, including the Guadeloupe population. Gene presence-absence analyses further revealed differences in functional potential between Guadeloupe and Stechlin cells across five functional annotation categories including PFAM, KEGG Orthologs, and CAZymes. Differences in genes associated with osmotic regulation, ion transport, carbohydrate degradation, and secretion systems suggest variation in functional potential related to environmental adaptation, interactions and resource utilization. No significant differences in functional potential between Guadeloupe morphotypes were found. Together, these marine genomes reveal genomic and functional differentiation from freshwater populations and suggest that intracellular diversity does not erase freshwater/saline population boundaries.

papers.title: HyperGenie: A method for predicting enzymatic gene essentiality using hypergraph neural networks and genome-scale metabolic models
papers.abstract: Identifying essential genes in bacteria is crucial for drug discovery and synthetic biology. Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) evaluated via flux balance analysis remain standard, yet they rely on the often-invalid premise that mutant strains optimize for maximum growth. Recent machine learning approaches circumvent this limitation using random forests or graph neural networks on mass flow graphs (MFGs). However, data-driven tools like random forests discard network topology, while graph-based tools like MFGs decompose multi-component biochemical reactions into pairwise interactions, misrepresenting complex stoichiometry and limiting interpretability. Furthermore, existing methods remain largely uncharacterised in data-scarce regimes and cross-environmental conditions. Here, we introduce HyperGenie, a framework that integrates genome-scale metabolic models with directed hypergraph neural networks by representing metabolites as nodes and reactions as hyperedges. Operating directly on wild-type flux features, HyperGenie eliminates post-knockout optimality assumptions, achieves a 13% PR-AUC improvement over prior objective-dependent methods, and matches computationally demanding, state-of-the-art flux-sampling baselines. Using HyperGenie to guide targeted growth curve assays, we identified latent essentiality misannotations across three genes in the benchmark iML1515 dataset, which we then reconciled and validated experimentally via PCR. In data-scarce regimes, HyperGenie retained robust predictive performance (> 90% PR-AUC) when trained on as little as 40% of the data. To isolate the value of hypergraph message passing, we benchmarked HyperGenie against an independent-reaction multilayer perceptron (MLPGenie) across diverse nutrient environments and uptake rates, where HyperGenie's hypergraph inductive bias yielded consistent accuracy gains (> 2% in glucose; > 4% across six alternative carbon sources). Notably, HyperGenie exhibits robust zero-shot cross-nutrient generalization, accurately forecasting gain-of-essentiality phenotypes on novel carbon sources, though loss-of-essentiality remains challenging. Finally, coupling hypergraph representations with SHAP attribution provides actionable mechanistic insights into metabolic rewiring, establishing a data-efficient, interpretable platform for discovering novel antibiotic targets.

papers.title: Stable isotope labeling reveals preferential ammonium acquisition by hydroponic lettuce under ambient and elevated CO2.
papers.abstract: Nitrogen (N) form acquired by plants reflects both physiological preference and environmentally mediated availability. Hydroponic controlled-environment agriculture (CEA) removes many constraints governing N availability yet remains predominantly reliant on nitrate (NO3-) nutrition. We used differential 15N stable-isotope labeling to quantify ammonium (NH4+) and NO3- acquisition by four lettuce (Lactuca sativa L.) cultivars grown hydroponically under terrestrial ambient (410 ppm) and spaceflight-relevant elevated (3000 ppm) CO2. Plants received equivalent concentrations of NH4+ and NO3-, with either N form selectively enriched with 15N during the final 24 h of growth. All cultivars exhibited significantly greater shoot 15N enrichment following 15NH4+ than 15NO3- labeling under both CO2 environments, demonstrating consistent preferential NH4+ acquisition. Preference magnitude varied among cultivars and broadly corresponded with biomass and total shoot N accumulation, driven predominantly by increased NH4+-derived enrichment rather than reduced NO3--derived enrichment. Elevated CO2 did not significantly alter N-form preference, although strong NH4+ preference persisted at 3000 ppm. These findings distinguish physiological acquisition preference from environmentally mediated N availability and provide a basis for reconsidering nitrate-dominant nutrition in terrestrial and space CEA, including integration with recycled reduced N.

papers.title: Extracellular matrix spatial ecosystems define stem-like niches and predict post-recurrence survival in glioblastomas
papers.abstract: Extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling is a hallmark of glioblastoma (GBM) yet has typically been studied through a reductionist lens, as individual genes or pathways rather than large scale, spatially integrated analyses coordinated with biological states. Focusing on whole matrisome gene expression, we identified three reproducible and spatially coherent ECM transcriptional programs, termed Homeostatic, Stress, and Fibrous, that were associated with specific microenvironmental functions and neoplastic cell states, with the strongest association noted between Homeostatic ECM and neoplastic quiescent stem cell-like (QSC) niches. Ligand-receptor analyses identified FGF1 and BGN as candidate ECM-driven regulators of QSC. In an independent longitudinal bulk transcriptomic cohort, ECM-based models outperformed traditional clinical and biomarker variables for predicting post-recurrence survival, with elevated Homeostatic ECM activity associated with improved post-recurrence survival, while MGMT promoter methylation no longer remained prognostic. Overall, these findings establish ECM organization as a clinically relevant dimension of GBM biology and nominate ECM-associated signaling as candidate therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Focused ultrasound-enhanced carboplatin delivery improves radiotherapy response and survival in a preclinical glioblastoma model
papers.abstract: Rationale Glioblastoma is highly resistant to conventional therapies due to the limited penetration of chemotherapeutics across the blood-brain and blood-tumor barriers (BBB, BTB). Although platinum-based drugs show strong cytotoxic and radiosensitizing properties in several cancers, their inability to achieve therapeutic concentrations within the central nervous system (CNS) severely limits their efficacy in brain tumors. This study investigated whether focused ultrasound (FUS)-mediated BBB/BTB disruption combined with intravenous carboplatin and stereotactic radiotherapy could improve drug delivery, tumor control, and survival in a preclinical glioblastoma model. Methods F98 glioma-bearing rats were treated with a single dose of 15 Gy radiation therapy (RT), carboplatin only, carboplatin + RT, FUS + carboplatin or FUS + carboplatin + RT. FUS-mediated permeabilization was confirmed by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and platinum accumulation was quantified by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry and synchrotron X-ray fluorescence. Tumor progression and microenvironmental changes were monitored using multiparametric MRI (diffusion, perfusion, and vascular permeability), followed by voxel-wise clustering analysis and histopathological validation. Results The FUS + carboplatin + RT group demonstrated the strongest therapeutic benefit, compared to all other treatment groups, yielding up to a 122% increase in median survival relative to the untreated group. This treatment also reduced necrotic core expansion and induced a transient increase in tumor perfusion, suggesting improved vascular function. FUS enhanced carboplatin delivery to both the tumor and peritumoral brain, with platinum distribution closely correlating with MRI signal enhancement. Voxel-wise clustering of multiparametric MRI identified biologically distinct tumor regions that were subsequently validated by immunohistochemistry. Conclusion The combination of FUS-mediated carboplatin delivery and radiotherapy represents a safe, non-invasive strategy that enhances drug delivery and improves survival in an aggressive preclinical model of glioblastoma. By overcoming a major limitation of current therapies, this approach shows promising potential for clinical translation. Keywords Glioblastoma, Focused Ultrasound, Blood-Brain Barrier, Chemotherapy, Radiotherapy

papers.title: Tumor-responsive AAV arms cancer cells to enhance CAR-T cell therapy in solid tumors
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T-cell therapy remains limited in solid tumors by the scarcity of suitable target antigens and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Here, we developed a tumor-responsive recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV) strategy that harnesses aberrant NF-{kappa}B activity to establish a shared synthetic CAR target across tumor types. Using an NF-{kappa}B-responsive decoy minimal promoter (DMP), rAAV-SA drove tumor-preferential surface expression of a synthetic antigen (SA), enabling antigen-dependent CAR-T-cell activation, degranulation, and cytotoxicity. Systemic rAAV-SA delivery combined with CAR-T cells produced antitumor activity in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) and colorectal cancer xenograft models. We subsequently engineered rAAV-ARMS (antigen redirection and multifunctional secreted effectors), integrating SA expression with tumor-local production of an IL-15/IL-15R sushi-domain fusion, CXCL10, and IFN-{gamma}. Compared with antigen redirection alone, rAAV-ARMS enhanced CAR-T-cell-mediated killing in three-dimensional tumor spheroids and, in a TNBC xenograft model, increased intratumoral T-cell accumulation and improved the efficacy of intravenously administered CAR-T cells, without overt systemic toxicity under the conditions examined. These findings establish a tumor-programmed platform for target-redirected universal CAR-T-cell therapy in solid tumors.

papers.title: Ventricular proximity associates with survival and immune remodelling in glioblastoma
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma is clinically and molecularly heterogeneous, yet whether its position relative to the lateral ventricles shapes tumour biology remains unclear. Here we measured tumour ventricle distance in 57 patients with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma and combined survival analysis with RNA sequencing, whole-genome sequencing, proteomics and multiplex immunofluorescence. Proximity to the ventricles was associated with shorter survival. Ventricle-proximal tumours lacked a distinct genomic driver but displayed an inflammatory yet immunoregulatory profile: antigen-presentation, leukocyte-activation and cytokine programmes coexisted with checkpoint and immunosuppressive transcripts, and proteomics revealed concordant complement and myeloid signals. In tissue, these tumours tended to show more Ki67-positive cells and proliferating SOX2-positive stem-like cells, suggesting increased plasticity of the stem-like compartment, without more CD4- or CD8a-positive lymphocytes. Ventricular proximity thus marks a clinically adverse context with a distinct immune-inflammatory profile, providing a framework for validation and patient stratification.

papers.title: The intestinal microbiome shapes responses to the GD2/GD3 cancer vaccine in children with high-risk neuroblastoma
papers.abstract: The intestinal microbiome influences vaccine responses, but its role in therapeutic cancer vaccination remains largely unexplored. We investigated the gut microbiome, vaccine immunogenicity and clinical outcomes in 137 children with high-risk neuroblastoma receiving GD2/GD3 vaccination with oral b-glucan. Microbiome-perturbing antibiotic exposure was associated with inferior progression-free survival (PFS). Among patients vaccinated in first remission, higher a-diversity and enrichment of Lachnospiraceae, including Blautia, were associated with higher anti-GD2 IgG1 responses, while higher Clostridia abundance was associated with superior PFS. Patients had microbiome profiles resembling those of chronologically younger healthy children, consistent with delayed microbiome maturation. A greater discrepancy between patients' chronological age and the age of microbiome-matched healthy children was associated with inferior PFS among patients in first remission. In a complementary mouse model, antibiotic treatment impaired vaccine-induced anti-GD2 IgG responses and accelerated tumor growth. Together, these findings support a role for the intestinal microbiome in therapeutic cancer vaccine responses and identify microbiome maturation as a clinically relevant feature in pediatrics.

papers.title: Large haploblocks underlie rapid, repeatable adaptation during evolutionary rescue
papers.abstract: Evolutionary rescue can prevent population extinction following abrupt environmental change, but the genetic architectures that enable rapid adaptation under simultaneous strong selection and severe demographic bottlenecks remain poorly resolved. In particular, rescue may rely on either dispersed adaptive variants or clusters of tightly linked alleles that can respond to selection despite strong drift. We investigated the genetic architecture of evolutionary rescue in Callosobruchus maculatus, the cowpea seed beetle, following a shift to lentil, a novel and stressful host. To do so, we combined experimental evolution, whole-genome sequencing, backcross introgression, early-generation genomic sampling, association mapping, and transcriptomics. Initial adaptation produced widespread genomic differentiation, but backcrossing localized evidence for adaptive variation primarily to large regions on chromosomes 1 and 9. These regions contained large haploblocks with patterns consistent with suppressed recombination, possibly due to structural variation. On chromosome 9, a rare haplotype increased from approximately 0.5% to 48% in a single generation in one genetic background, consistent with extremely strong selection (s {approx} 0.9995). On chromosome 1, a 14 Mb haploblock contained nearly all genetic variation for two fitness-related traits and was associated with differential gene expression. Across genetic backgrounds, chromosome 1 was repeatedly implicated in adaptation, whereas lines from one source population additionally involved chromosome 9. Together, these results show that evolutionary rescue can rely on large, non-recombining haploblocks, providing a mechanism by which clustered genetic architectures can respond rapidly and repeatably despite severe population bottlenecks.

papers.title: The origin and diversity of insulin sequences and structures in nature
papers.abstract: The diversification of peptide signaling systems has been a major driver of metazoan evolution and biological complexity. The insulin superfamily, which includes insulins, insulin-like peptides, relaxins, and insulin-like growth factors, is an ancient group of peptide hormones that regulate development, growth, metabolism, and reproduction across Metazoa. Yet our understanding of the evolutionary origin of insulin signaling and the full extent of insulin superfamily diversity remain incomplete, particularly in invertebrates. Here, we performed a large-scale sequence and structural investigation of the insulin superfamily by mining public databases with sequence- and structure-based computational analyses to build a final dataset of 7,020 insulin-family sequences. Insulin-like peptides were present in all metazoan lineages except Porifera and Ctenophora. The absence of an identifiable canonical insulin ligand in Porifera is particularly intriguing because insulin receptors are present, raising questions about the receptors ancestral function and the evolutionary origin of its ligand. We further identified 12 distinct structural classes of insulin-superfamily peptides, with the greatest diversity in invertebrates, marking these lineages as a major source of insulin scaffold innovation. Together, these findings provide new insights into the origin and diversification of insulin signaling, establish a framework for understanding insulin superfamily evolution, and offer a resource for the discovery and engineering of therapeutic insulin analogs inspired by natural diversity.

papers.title: The evolution of the HIV-1 integrase through constraints from folding stability and functional interactions
papers.abstract: The rapid evolution of human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) facilitates the emergence and fixation of drug-resistance mutations (DRMs). Although variants carrying DRMs gain a selective advantage under antiretroviral treatment, these mutations may compromise protein fitness, affecting viral replication efficiency and shaping evolutionary trajectories. Understanding the emergence, fixation, and fitness effects of DRMs is therefore essential for predicting evolutionary outcomes and optimizing therapies. Here, we investigated the evolution of the HIV-1 integrase, a key antiretroviral target, and the influence of common DRMs by analyzing folding stability, DNA substrate binding affinity, and structural properties across integrase variants using long molecular dynamics simulations combined with protein phylogenetic inference. DRMs generally altered protein folding stability and protein-DNA interactions to a marginal extent, due to their number, position, and physicochemical properties. Several DRMs altered catalytic site geometry, including alteration of magnesium coordination within the catalytic triad and modulation of enzymatic activity by changes in flexibility of the 140-149 loop involved in substrate binding, while others had minor effects on DNA binding. Over long evolutionary timescales, temporal fluctuations in folding stability and DNA-binding affinity were observed, potentially driven by alternating diversification and selection regimes at molecular and population levels. We conclude that HIV-1 integrase evolves under marginal stability, allowing structural variation that supports adaptation while preserving essential activity, which should be considered in predictions of structural evolutionary trajectories. Together, integrating biophysical properties with evolutionary modeling provides a robust framework for understanding how structural constraints influence the fixation of adaptive mutations.

papers.title: p53 supports healthy aging
papers.abstract: p53 is a master regulator of cellular stress responses that is also implicated in the aging process. Its role in aging is often considered an example of antagonistic pleiotropy (AP), where it acts beneficially as a tumor suppressor early in life, but detrimentally in late life, for example by driving accumulation of stress-associated, pro-inflammatory senescent cells. However, the causal role of p53 in aging is not well-defined, and the AP model has not been definitively tested through loss- of-function studies. Here we show, contrary to the prediction of AP, that p53 promotes healthy aging in mouse liver by suppressing excessive inflammation and maintaining metabolic function. Multimodal RNA, protein, epigenetic and spatial profiling at the single-cell level in aged mouse liver confirmed age-dependent increase in p53 pathway activation. Hepatocyte-specific knockout of p53 in livers of aged mice, but not of young mice, increased inflammation and immune infiltration. Mechanistically, p53 suppressed DNA replication stress and DNA damage, known precursors to inflammatory signaling. In aged hepatocytes, p53 also directly targeted and maintained expression of metabolic genes, and knockout of p53 sensitized aged mice to metabolic stress-induced liver damage. Complementing these loss-of-function data, pharmacological activation of p53 with the small-molecule MDM2 inhibitor HDM201 in aged mice reversed age-associated suppression of metabolic genes, decreased age-associated inflammation and delayed onset of frailty. These results identify p53 activity in aged tissue as protective rather than degenerative. Importantly, this protective function is pharmacologically targetable, potentially for the benefit of healthy aging in humans.

papers.title: Comparative chemogenetic profiling of Hedgehog pathway inhibitors reveals class-specific genetic modifiers
papers.abstract: Chemogenetic profiling is a powerful method to dissect compound-gene interactions and to reveal a compound's mechanism of action and possible resistance mechanisms. Here, we extended the use of chemogenetic profiling beyond cytotoxic compounds to classify non-toxic inhibitors of the Hedgehog signaling pathway. We performed Hedgehog pathway-focused genetic screens in NIH/3T3 mouse fibroblasts using two chemically distinct inhibitors each of Smoothened (SMO) and BET bromodomain proteins. The resulting chemogenetic profiles revealed class-specific modifiers, with loss of Mosmo conferring resistance to SMO inhibitors, and loss of Paxip1 conferring resistance to BET bromodomain inhibitors. Beyond these compound-specific effects, we show how loss of Nf2, Paxip1, or Mosmo differentially impacts Hedgehog pathway transduction upstream, at the level of the cilium, and/or downstream, at the level of transcription. Together, the Mosmo- and Paxip1-knockout lines provide new tools for epistasis mapping, and the profiling strategy a route to mechanism-of-action studies for inhibitors of ciliary signaling.

papers.title: Selenite transport by SLC26A6 contributes to redox homeostasis and ferroptosis resistance
papers.abstract: Selenium is an essential micronutrient widely found in dietary supplements and fortified foods and is required for selenoprotein synthesis and function. Although the molecular mechanisms of selenium-dependent selenoprotein translation are well understood, its uptake mechanisms remain only partially characterized. Using a CRISPR-based loss-of-function screen, we identify the solute carrier SLC26A6 as a direct selenite transporter. Using biochemical, cellular, and in vivo studies, we show that SLC26A6 directly transports selenite and promotes selenoprotein translation, redox homeostasis, and ferroptosis resistance. Additionally, we report the first human-specific SLC26A6 inhibitor and determine the structure of the SLC26A6-inhibitor complex by cryo-electron microscopy. These findings identify a previously uncharacterized route of inorganic selenium uptake and establish SLC26A6 as a pharmacologically tractable determinant of selenoprotein synthesis, redox homeostasis, and ferroptosis resistance.

papers.title: MTCH2 drives metabolic remodeling in muscle satellite cells via mitochondrial fatty acid utilization
papers.abstract: Muscle satellite cell (MuSC) differentiation into myoblasts underpins skeletal muscle regeneration by supporting myofiber repair and formation. This process involves extensive metabolic remodeling from glycolysis to mitochondrial oxidative metabolism. Although this switch is required for proper MuSC differentiation, its molecular regulators remain unclear. Here, we identify mitochondrial carrier homolog 2 (MTCH2) as a regulator of this remodeling. MTCH2 contributes preferentially to MuSC differentiation rather than proliferation and supports mitochondrial respiration, particularly under a low-glucose condition. Loss of Mtch2 fragments mitochondria and suppresses respiration associated with fatty acid {beta}-oxidation. Notably, MTCH2-dependent fatty acid utilization appears largely independent of carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1 (CPT1). Furthermore, skeletal muscle regeneration is impaired in MuSC-specific Mtch2 conditional knockout mice. Together, these findings establish MTCH2 as a regulator of mitochondrial metabolic remodeling in MuSCs and highlight its context-dependent roles in cellular metabolism and function.

papers.title: NRF2 regulates a lipofuscin-like granule cycle through autophagy-dependent clearance in retinal pigment epithelium
papers.abstract: Lysosomal dysfunction in retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells is one pathological aspect of retinal degenerative disorders, which contribute to the buildup of autofluorescent undegraded materials such as lipofuscin. A comprehensive understanding of lipofuscin biology remains a critical gap in the field. Here, we explore the cell biology of lipofuscin-like autofluorescent granules (AFGs) within RPE cells and the potential of nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) activation to promote its clearance in human RPE cells. Under steady-state conditions we find that photoreceptor outer segments (POS) phagocytosis by the RPE is sufficient to trigger NRF2 activation, suggesting a feedback mechanism that links phagocytic activity with cytoprotective stress responses. RPE fed with excess POS accumulate lipofuscin-like autofluorescent granules (AFG) within hours, a measure of lysosomal dysfunction. These AFGs gradually loose connection with the endocytic system and remain as ''storage granules'' within RPE. Pre-treatment or delayed pharmacological activation of NRF2 with dimethyl fumarate (DMF) significantly decrease accumulation of AFGs, suggesting improved clearance mechanisms. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of autophagy totally abolish these effects. Similarly, compromised autophagy also abolished the clearance effects observed with inhibition of the mTOR pathway. Collectively, these results suggest a 3-step lipofuscin cycle within the RPE (formation, storage and clearance), provide mechanistic evidence that autophagy is an essential process for the clearance of AFGs and that NRF2-activation and other stimulators of autophagy may represent novel therapeutic strategies to restore RPE homeostasis and mitigate retinal degeneration.

papers.title: Depolymerases unmask a conserved receptor to enable phage control of capsulated Acinetobacter baumannii
papers.abstract: We characterized bacteriophage Abs1 that infects clinical Acinetobacter baumannii isolates via the highly prevalent and conserved outer-membrane protein receptor, OprC. However, phage Abs1 is unable to infect capsulated A. baumannii strains as the capsule prevents phage access to its underlying receptor. To circumvent this, we combined phage Abs1 with recombinant depolymerases targeting the major A. baumannii capsule types. In a murine bacteremia model, this combination significantly reduced bacterial burden caused by diverse, capsulated A. baumannii strains.

papers.title: Choosing between Glycolysis and Cholera: identifying glycolipid- and enzyme-based markers of extracellular vesicles in non-model organisms
papers.abstract: The lack of universal markers for extracellular vesicles (EVs) is delaying progress in the field, especially research using non-model organisms. To develop effective options for the detection of EVs, we explored glycolipid-based and protein-based markers. In this study, we show that cholera toxin subunit B (CTxb), which targets the glycosphingolipid GM1 in vertebrates, also binds to EVs from various non-model organisms enabling detection. However, whilst CTxb selectively detect EVs from cell culture and parasite media, it is unsuitable for complex biofluids, such as serum and plasma due to cross-reactivity with high- and low-density lipoproteins. Additionally, we show that the universally conserved glycolytic enzyme enolase is found in EVs from phylogenetically distant species. Multiple highly conserved regions exist across human and several representative non-model organism orthologues, enabling detection of EVs from non-model organism using antibodies against human enolase. Furthermore, the conserved enzymatic activity of enolase enables detection of EVs using an enzymatic assay. Together CTxb and enolase provide a tandem approach for detection of EVs from non-model organisms by targeting different, conserved components of EVs.

papers.title: Enhancing violacein production in an Antarctic bacterial strain: New opportunities for biomedical use
papers.abstract: Violacein is a valuable bioactive metabolite produced by diverse bacteria, including the Antarctic isolate Janthinobacterium sp. UV13. Despite its broad therapeutic potential, large-scale production in native producers is hindered by low yields and the concurrent synthesis of exopolysaccharides, which increases downstream processing complexity and costs. This study employed a sequential statistical approach to optimize culture parameters, enhancing violacein productivity while minimizing exopolysaccharides production in UV13. The methodology included carbon and nitrogen source screening, a Plackett Burman design and a concentration response optimization, followed by chemical inducers evaluation. Results demonstrated that sucrose was an effective carbon source (violacein yield: 32.75 mg/L). Inorganic nitrogen significantly favored violacein synthesis (yield: 28 mg/L, p < 0.05) over organic alternatives which reduced violacein yields 3.4 to 4.2 fold. A single factor central composite design of ammonium sulfate concentration yielded a formulation producing 75.8 mg/L of violacein with an exopolysaccharide titer of 0.91 mg/L. Furthermore, tryptophan was the better inducer, increasing violacein production 2.2 fold (p < 0.05) while simultaneously decreasing exopolysaccharides formation 4.5 fold. The new formulated medium significantly outperformed previously reported conditions, demonstrating that parameter manipulation unlocks UV13 biosynthetic potential for scalable violacein production.

papers.title: Yin-Yang homeodynamics of Nrf1 and Nrf2: coupling antioxidant defense to redox recovery bistability under persistent stress
papers.abstract: This work systematically articulates the Yin-Yang homeodynamics coordination between Nrf1 and Nrf2, resolving the longstanding core paradox in redox biology of why robust Nrf2-mediated antioxidant activation frequently fails to fully eliminate unresolved oxidative stress and re-establish sustained redox homeostasis. Integrating multi-omic expression profiles from human HepG2 cells and primary murine hepatocytes, we constructed an 11-variable endogenous regulatory network model, demonstrating that Nrf2 exclusively mediates transient acute stress attenuation responses, while Nrf1 functions as the non-redundant upstream organiser that supplies the indispensable preconditions for definitive stress resolution via three irreplaceable homeostatic axes: organelle integrity maintenance, proteasome functional recovery, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) cholesterol steady-state handling. Their coupled regulatory interactions generate a bistable configuration demarcated by an index-1 saddle point, partitioning the physiological state space into native low-stress homeostasis and the previously uncharacterised persistent-stress attractor. Once self-amplified unresolved endogenous stress generation reaches dynamic flux balance with Nrf2-dependent clearance at an elevated burden level, the system becomes irreversibly locked in this persistent high-burden equilibrium, and cannot spontaneously return to native homeostatic status even after the initiating upstream disturbance has been fully corrected. Collectively, this study fundamentally delineates the clear functional division between transient antioxidant activation and durable redox recovery during Nrf1/Nrf2 homeodynamics, hence providing a rigorous systems-level theoretical framework to guide future translational interventions targeting redox homeostasis restoration.

papers.title: Mapping the Plant Extracellular Proteome: From Fraction-Specific Secretion Patterns to Experimental Guidelines
papers.abstract: Proteins operating beyond the plasma membrane are central to how plants build and remodel their cell walls, acquire and redistribute nutrients, coordinate developmental processes, and communicate between cells and tissues. Moreover, the reach of this extracellular proteome extends beyond the plant itself, with root and seed exudates shaping the rhizosphere and spermosphere by providing molecular signals and resources that influence microbial communities even before pathogens or symbionts establish direct contact with the plant surface. The extracellular space is therefore a dynamic biological interface connecting processes within the plant to interactions with the soil, microbiome, and broader environment. Despite this central role, the plant extracellular proteome remains fragmented across experimental approaches. Here, we review current techniques for the collection and purification of major plant extracellular fractions and use a uniform prediction pipeline to assess representative publicly available datasets. This analysis reveals consistent fraction-specific patterns in predicted secretion-class composition, with putative unconventional-secretion candidates exceeding canonical candidates in most fractions. We then present a decision tree linking biological questions to appropriate collection and fractionation strategies, together with complementary experimental criteria for assessing extracellular origin that extend beyond sequence-based prediction. Together, these resources provide a framework for interpreting existing extracellular proteomic datasets and for designing future studies that account for the biological distinctness of individual extracellular fractions. They are intended both as an entry point to plant extracellular proteomics and as a reference framework for improving the biological interpretation and comparability of studies across this diverse extracellular landscape.

papers.title: Plant growth, biomass, and nitrogen utilization are impacted by mutations in C4 PEPCK1 in maize
papers.abstract: Efficient photosynthesis is crucial to agricultural productivity and can be constrained by the plant carbon-nitrogen balance, offering an opportunity for genetic improvement. Furthermore, soil N availability limits grain yields, and crops require substantial N fertilizer to be productive. In C4 plants, carbon-concentrating mechanisms respond to decreased soil nitrogen and share molecular intermediates with N metabolism. Maize, one of the most widely grown crops globally, uses a combination of two C4 photosynthetic pathways. Most carbon fixation occurs through the NADP-malic enzyme (NADP-ME) pathway, yet some fixation is also thought to occur via phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase (PEPCK). However, genetic evidence for the contribution of PEPCK is lacking. Here, we used a transposon-based mutagenesis approach to study the function of the C4 isoform of PEPCK1 in maize. The C4 pathway intermediate aspartate accumulated to high concentrations in the leaves of the pepck1-2::Ds knock-down mutant, providing genetic support for the PEPCK secondary pathway as a complement to the dominant NADP-ME shuttle in maize. Field experiments over multiple seasons in either N-limiting or N-sufficient soils demonstrated the pepck1::Ds mutants produced higher vegetative and grain biomass without changes in leaf photosynthetic rates or parameters. This study confirms that PEPCK1 catalyzes the decarboxylation of carbon shuttled as aspartate, as an alternative route to decarboxylation by NADP-ME in a nominally NADP-ME subtype C4 species maize, providing clear genetic support for two-pathway operation. Further, the greater resilience and N-responsiveness of mutant plants are valuable traits for sustainable and subsistence farming in the future.
